verdict.rationale: Restate is a durable execution engine built for unattended work. Its docs cover durable timers for sleeping, scheduling, delayed messages and cron-like patterns. They also cover async invocations with guaranteed exactly-once execution, durable webhooks, Kafka-triggered handlers, infinite retries with backoff, and suspension of long-running agents when idle. Together these let code-defined automations and agents run autonomously in the background and recover from failures. Missing for 10: a native first-class cron or recurring-schedule feature (docs only say you can 'implement patterns like cron jobs'), and independent or hands-on corroboration that background automations run reliably in practice.
